name: Elm
summary: The language The Elm Architecture comes from, and the reference every other entry is graded against.
notes: Only elm/* packages may define effect managers, so a new kind of Cmd or Sub (websockets, a new browser API) goes through ports.
Frameworks written in Elm (elm-pages, elm-land) are libraries of this column, not entries of their own.

name: Gren
summary: A fork of Elm with its own package set, which also runs on Node for command line tools and servers.
notes: Programs on Node use the same Model, update and subscriptions without a view.

name: Lamdera
summary: Elm on both sides: a second TEA loop runs on the server, with typed messages between frontend and backend.
notes: The backend has its own Model, update and subscriptions; data sync and migrations are part of the platform.

name: Miso
summary: A Haskell front-end framework with the Elm shape, plus components, server-side rendering and hydration.
notes: Components with their own model, update, view and subscriptions since 1.9.
Subscriptions are user-defined: createSub acquires and releases their resources when a component mounts and unmounts.
update schedules effects with io; it does not run them.

name: Monomer
summary: A native desktop GUI toolkit for Haskell, inspired by Elm.
notes: handleEvent returns responses: model updates, Task (one result) and Producer (a stream of events).

name: gi-gtk-declarative
summary: Declarative GTK for Haskell; its app-simple package runs an Elm-style loop.
notes: update returns a transition with an IO action that may produce the next event; input streams feed events from outside.

name: Flame
summary: A fast and simple PureScript framework inspired by The Elm Architecture.
notes: Often called the most Elm-like PureScript option.
Mostly maintained by one developer.

name: Elmish (PureScript)
summary: The Elm Architecture in PureScript, rendering through React.
notes: Maintained by CollegeVine and used in production there.

name: Halogen
summary: A component framework for PureScript: as powerful as TEA, with components, queries and slots, but not shaped like it.
notes: handleAction runs effects directly in the HalogenM monad instead of returning them as data.
Subscriptions are started imperatively from an emitter.
Listed as a superset for its power; a strict reading of the rubric would move it to the adjacent page.

name: Pux
summary: An early Elm-style framework for PureScript, kept for its history.

name: Spork
summary: Elm-like apps in PureScript on a fast virtual DOM, close to Elm in speed.

name: Elmish (Fable)
summary: The Elm Architecture for F#, compiled to JavaScript by Fable; the base of a large family of F# frameworks.
notes: Keyed, model-dependent subscriptions since v4 (Program.withSubscription), which users can define themselves.
The runtime is renderer-agnostic: the entries below reuse it for WebAssembly, desktop, mobile and terminal.

name: Bolero
summary: Elmish on Blazor: F# web apps in WebAssembly.
notes: Can render on the server and stream updates, through Blazor.

name: Elmish.WPF
summary: Elmish for Windows desktop apps, with the view in WPF XAML bound to the model.
notes: The view is static XAML with bindings, not a function that returns a view tree.

name: Fabulous
summary: Declarative native mobile and desktop apps in F#, on .NET MAUI and Avalonia.

name: Avalonia.FuncUI
summary: Cross-platform desktop apps in F# on Avalonia, with an Elmish integration and its own component model.
notes: The Elmish runtime comes from Avalonia.FuncUI.Elmish; components with local state are offered beside it.

name: Terminal.Gui.Elmish
summary: Elmish over Terminal.Gui, with a view DSL in the style of Feliz.
notes: A port to Terminal.Gui v2 is published as OnurGumus.Terminal.Gui.Elmish.

name: bucklescript-tea
summary: A close port of the Elm API to OCaml and ReScript, continued as rescript-tea.
notes: The original repository is no longer active; forks under the rescript-tea name continue it.

name: ocaml-vdom
summary: Elm-style virtual DOM apps in OCaml through js_of_ocaml, by LexiFi.

name: Mint Tea
summary: A terminal UI framework for OCaml on the Riot runtime, inspired by Bubble Tea.
notes: Leaves is its set of reusable components, and Spices its styling library.

name: Lustre
summary: The Elm Architecture in Gleam, in the browser and on the server, with universal components.
notes: Server components run the update loop on the Erlang target and patch the DOM over a socket; since 5.5 they can join supervision trees.
Components can be registered as custom elements.
There is no subscriptions function: long-running sources are effects that keep dispatching.

name: Shore
summary: A terminal UI framework for Gleam following The Elm Architecture, on the Erlang runtime.
notes: Needs Erlang/OTP 28 or later.

name: Teashop
summary: A Gleam terminal framework inspired by Bubble Tea and Mint Tea.

name: gleamtea
summary: A terminal UI framework for Gleam on top of beamtea, a Bubble Tea for Erlang.
notes: beamtea itself can be used from Erlang directly.

name: Ratatouille
summary: A declarative terminal UI kit for Elixir, built on The Elm Architecture.
notes: Its app behaviour has init, update, render and subscribe(model).

name: Tyrian
summary: An Elm-inspired UI library for Scala 3 and Scala.js, by the makers of the Indigo game engine.
notes: Began as a fork of Scalm.
A bridge lets a Tyrian app and an Indigo game talk through their messages.
Its docs have a page on how it differs from Elm.
Moved in 2025 to the indigoengine monorepo with Indigo; the old repository is archived.

name: Indigo
summary: A functional game engine for Scala.js whose loop is a variation of The Elm Architecture.
notes: Frame driven: updateModel returns an Outcome that carries the next model and the events to send; the view is a scene.
Moved in 2025 to the indigoengine monorepo with Tyrian; the old repository is archived.

name: Scalm
summary: Elm-inspired Scala.js library, the ancestor of Tyrian.

name: react-tea-cup
summary: The Elm Architecture for React and TypeScript, with tea-cup-fp for Cmd, Sub, Task and Port.
notes: ProgramWithNav turns URL changes into messages.
Renders in the terminal through Ink: the realworld example has a TUI admin built on it.
Component packages (forms, router, drawer, pagination) live in tea-cup-package.

name: Foldkit
summary: A TypeScript frontend framework built on Effect: one Model, one update, and side effects as values the runtime runs.
notes: All or nothing by design: no React interop and no way around Effect.
Purity is kept by convention; the compiler cannot stop an effect inside update the way Elm does.

name: elm-ts
summary: A port of The Elm Architecture to TypeScript on fp-ts, RxJS and React.
notes: tea-effect presents itself as its spiritual successor.

name: tea-effect
summary: The Elm Architecture on Effect, with React hooks; started in 2026 as a successor to elm-ts.

name: @typescript-tea/core
summary: A framework-agnostic TEA core for TypeScript, with effects as data and the view left to React or another library.

name: react-elmish
summary: The Elmish pattern for React, with commands and subscriptions.

name: Hyperapp
summary: A tiny JavaScript framework whose actions return new state with effects, and whose subscriptions are a function of the state.
notes: Untyped: messages are action functions rather than a closed union.

name: Ferp
summary: Elm-style state, effects and subscriptions for JavaScript, in the browser or in Node.

name: iced
summary: A cross-platform, renderer-agnostic GUI library for Rust, inspired by Elm.
notes: update returns a Task; subscription(&self) is a function of the state.

name: libcosmic
summary: The toolkit of the COSMIC desktop, built on iced, with app, applet and theming layers on top.

name: Relm4
summary: An idiomatic GUI library for Rust on GTK4, inspired by Elm, with components and workers.
notes: Commands run async work and send their result back as a message.

name: Sauron
summary: A Rust web framework heavily inspired by Elm, with the view built from plain function calls.

name: Seed
summary: A Rust frontend framework whose apps mimic the structure of The Elm Architecture.
notes: Commands go through an orders object passed to update; streams stand in for subscriptions.

name: Draco
summary: An early Rust and WebAssembly library for Elm-style web apps.

name: tears
summary: A TEA framework for terminal apps on ratatui, inspired by Elm, iced and Bubble Tea, with async commands.

name: hojicha
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal UIs in Rust on ratatui, inspired by Bubble Tea.
notes: GPL-3.0 licensed.
Its repository is on a Gitea host that needs a sign-in to view, so the site links its docs instead.

name: osteak
summary: The Elm Architecture for ratatui, with a built-in runner or your own event loop.

name: teatui
summary: An experimental Elm-like layer over ratatui that keeps mutation to a minimum.
notes: Moved from GitHub to Codeberg in 2026; the GitHub repository is archived.

name: Bubble Tea
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in Go, with the largest TUI ecosystem around it.
notes: No subscriptions function: a subscription is a Cmd that blocks on a channel or reschedules itself.
Program.Send feeds messages from outside the program.
Bubbles (components), Lip Gloss (styling) and Huh (forms) are built on it; v2 moved to charm.land/bubbletea/v2.

name: The Composable Architecture
summary: State, actions and reducers that return effects, for SwiftUI and UIKit apps, with composition and exhaustive testing.
notes: Reducers return Effect values; long-running effects with cancellation stand in for subscriptions.
TestStore checks every state change and every effect a test causes.
Dependencies are injected and replaced in tests.

name: Mobius.swift
summary: The Swift port of Mobius by Spotify: a TEA loop that feeds any view layer.
notes: Headless: there is no view function; the loop drives UIKit or SwiftUI through a connection.

name: Mobius
summary: The Spotify framework for state and side effects, used in its Android apps.
notes: update returns the next model with effects, which effect handlers run.
An EventSource feeds events from outside the loop.
Headless: the view is any Android UI connected to the loop.

name: Mobius.kt
summary: Mobius for Kotlin Multiplatform: update functions in common Kotlin, run on every target.

name: Elmslie
summary: TEA for Kotlin with first-class Android support, by Vivid Money.
notes: Modular: core, Android lifecycle, RxJava and Jetpack Compose artifacts.

name: Tea-bag
summary: A TEA implementation for Kotlin built on coroutines.

name: Dartea
summary: An MVU engine for Flutter inspired by TEA and Elmish.

name: mvu_layer
summary: Elm-inspired state management for Flutter: update is the only place that changes the model.

name: mvu_flutter
summary: A fuller Elm-style implementation for Flutter, with detailed docs.

name: Milo
summary: The Elm Architecture for terminal apps in Python, with commands, sagas and subscriptions (ticks, terminal resize).
notes: To check: whether commands are returned from the reducer or started beside it (a saga runner would make it TEA-adjacent).
